flags.message: Footprint is now settled by answer at the drawing's 22'-11" × 11'-8" clear (267 sqft), so every proposal/JBD quantity built on 294 sqft (slab, excavation, roof area, rafters, gutter removal, perimeter) runs ~9% high; only the paver demo area stays at the proposal's 294 because it measures the existing field, not the new slab.

Knee wall is settled at ~3'-4" with lap siding outside and beadboard inside, but the JBD prices a 2' wall with a $345 'white vinyl finish' line and no beadboard or siding — the wall is 67% taller (~107 sqft per face, ~214 sqft of cladding) and carries two finish systems the JBD never priced, so its 48h/$1,713 screen section is wrong in both directions (60 LF too long, 2' too short, vinyl instead of siding+beadboard).

Neither the proposal nor the JBD carries paint or finish for the lap siding, beadboard, or the white-rendered rafters/trim, yet the drawings show all of them painted and the chimney brick 'painted same color as main house' — either primed/finished stock is assumed or an unpriced paint scope exists; sizing should not add paint hours without a source.

Post count is settled at 7-9 (carried 8) but the JBD prices 5 posts and zero turned-down footings — post material, footing excavation/forming, and ~0.5-0.7 cy extra concrete are missing from the JBD concrete and framing sections, so its 42h/70h should not be read as covering them; the smaller slab happens to offset the missing footing volume so the 4.2 cy ready-mix now lands roughly right.

JBD carries $0 permits and no inspection line items while the answer confirms a Johnson City building permit with framing and fireplace/chimney inspections — permit_items and bundled_inspections receive no JBD hours but must not be zero downstream; inspection holds gate framing close and fireplace veneer.

JBD roof-structure labor includes 'chimney-penetration framing', TL 8h for 10-3-2 chimney-height work, and $245 chimney roof flashing/storm collar, but the settled location and termination put the chimney outside the shed roof edge ending just above the low eave — that work reduces to a chase-to-eave counterflash detail, not a penetration or a tall chase.

The chimney-termination policy (cap just above the ~8' low eave, not above the shed roof's high side) sits below the shed roof plane within 10' horizontally, which is the geometry 10-3-2 normally forbids — the confirmed fireplace/chimney inspection is where this could be rejected, so sizing should not assume the chase height is final until the inspector or the firebox manufacturer's termination table signs off.

Gutter answer end-caps the existing run at the tie-in and leaves the downspout where it is, but no source says which side of the ~23' removed section the downspout sits on — if it was on the removed run, the remaining upstream gutter is capped with no outlet and someone will be adding a downspout that nobody has priced; if it was outside the tie-in, the work is a single end-cap and trivially small.

Roof structure 70h for a ~290 sqft single-plane shed roof with ~18 rafters, two beams, ~8 posts and 10 sheets of sheathing runs hot; a 3-person crew would normally frame and sheathe this in 2-2.5 days (~50h), and with the ledger replaced by a beam on posts and the eave tie-in limited to gutter removal plus one end-cap the only extra effort is post/beam setting.

Fireplace structure 98h (90h GL) is heavy now that the manufactured firebox + Class A pipe in a ~6'-wide framed chase terminating at the low eave is settled — a manufactured kit is typically a 3-4 day, 2-person install (~50-65h); the 98h only made sense against the masonry option that is now off the table.

Screened enclosure 48h is built on the wrong wall (60 LF × 2' vinyl); the governing ~32 LF × 3'-4" wall with lap siding, beadboard, screen frames, transom band, one door and trim is more work per foot but far fewer feet — net effort is probably comparable (2-person crew ~3 days), but the JBD's hours are coincidental, not derived.
Electrical 6h and $95 material carried for a scope confirmed zero-electrical with no rough-in — this collapses to 0h; the JBD's own PM notes anticipated this.

General conditions 30h includes 18h PM for fireplace-system and finish-selection coordination that is now complete per answers (all selections final, lead times known) — remaining PM effort is scheduling, permit pull, and inspection coordination, closer to 8-12h.

No roof pitch or beam/post sizing exists in any source (sized in-house per IRC tables, not yet done); roof area is carried as plan area (~290 sqft) with no slope factor, and the exact chase/cap height is undimensioned even though termination is settled at 'just above the low eave'.

Firebox + Class A kit lead time is 3-4 weeks and the kit dimensions drive the fireplace footing thickening and chase framing — with the 'no demo without materials' policy, the kit (or at least its spec sheet) must be in hand before the slab pour, which the JBD's ~5-6 wk duration does not account for.

Concrete patio is mapped to groundwork (foundation before framing) rather than concrete_landscape because it carries the fireplace footing and every post footing; downstream should expect no separate flatwork phase after the shell, and yard restoration is excluded by the JBD.

Screened enclosure now splits three ways with real work in each: framing (knee wall + screen frames) → structural_framing, exterior lap siding + trim → cladding_roof, interior beadboard + screening + door → interior_installs; the JBD's single 48h line cannot be apportioned from its own text, so any split is a judgment.

Fireplace structure and finish land on their dedicated components (fireplace_structure under Framing & Shell, fireplace_finish under Exterior Finishes); the finish component's Exterior Finishes home is a slight misfit since veneer/hearth/mantel are inside the screened porch and must follow the chimney inspection — downstream should not sequence it ahead of the chase inspection just because of the phase label.
